### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceApiAccess (10 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2f98458f404ccb30b57872a9fc28555983230977` — the merge of head `2019e190f5c40af31fbabccf6fb2d5a3fa612e28` into base `ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2f98458f404ccb30b57872a9fc28555983230977 && git checkout 2f98458f404ccb30b57872a9fc28555983230977
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 2019e190f5c40af31fbabccf6fb2d5a3fa612e28 && git checkout -B drift-repro ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 && git merge --no-ff 2019e190f5c40af31fbabccf6fb2d5a3fa612e28

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2019e190f5c40af31fbabccf6fb2d5a3fa612e28`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts, packages/rest/src/objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-op-exposure-object-read.test.ts, .changeset/27899-batch-op-exposure-object-read.md + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`loadObjectItem`, `loadObjectItems`, `MetaReadGateListSource`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`enforceApiAccess`, `objectItemReader`, `metaListSource`, `apiAccessDenialFromEnable`, the `BatchRouteHost` literal), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`getObject`, `resolveObjectKey`, `getItem`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts (`readMetaItemFace`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`readMetaItem` step 3 and its degraded arm), packages/spec/src/api/batch.zod.ts (`CrossObjectBatchOperationSchema`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the category list), scripts/adr-anchors/packages__rest__src__rest-server.ts.json

Read at 2026-10-30T05:29Z against the net diff `origin/main` (`ed0e71db`)`...2019e190` (7 files, +278/−46; the PR's file list is the same seven), card #27899 (body, triage 6514615922, claim 6514787457 with its seat amendment, dev report 6515574134), PR #27963's body, merged PR #27897 with its records 6513915701 / 6513977097 and ACCEPT 6514232261, and the head's check-runs. Face: `narrowing`, from the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema and no governed path in the file list. Adversarial read: the PR body, the dev report and the dispatch were inputs to test, not findings to adopt; triage's ruling taken as given, not re-ruled. This card is an API exposure gate: everything below is stated at rule level.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Every op kind of the cross-object batch now reads its object through the one read the `/data` gate uses, and refuses with the same envelope.** The spec's op schema (`CrossObjectBatchOperationSchema`) admits exactly `create`, `update`, `delete` (default `create`) on a non-empty `object` string, so the per-op loop in `batch-routes.ts` covers every op kind the door can parse. Each distinct `op.object` is read once through `this.loadObjectItem(p, environmentId, op.object)`; each distinct (object, action) is judged once, in op order; the first denial answers for the batch; the transaction has not opened. The denial is `apiAccessDenialFromEnable(obj.enable, op.object, 'bulk', { bulkChild: op.action })`, unchanged, and the per-object bulk routes call `enforceApiAccess(…, 'bulk', context, { bulkChild: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' })`, which reaches the same function with the same requested name: 404 `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` for `apiEnabled: false`, 405 `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` naming the failed conjunct for a whitelist that leaves `bulk` or the child out. Same status, same code, same body shape. Correct.
2. **The replacement read is the `/data` gate's read, byte for byte, not a sibling of it.** `enforceApiAccess` used to assemble `metaListSource` + `objectItemReader` and call `metaReadGate.loadObjectItem` inline; the diff moves that assembly into `RestServer#loadObjectItem(p, environmentId, name)` and makes `enforceApiAccess` call it, so the data door and the batch door cannot drift on which face or which envelope they read. `objectItemReader` prefers `getMetaItemForExecution`, else `getMetaItem`, else `undefined` (then `loadObjectItem` falls back to the list with its exact-name match, the one non-resolving arm, unchanged from #27897). Correct.
3. **The accept-set change is exactly the short-name alias set, and nothing else.** The by-name read's step 3 is `registry.getItem('object', name)` → `getObject(name)` → `resolveObjectKey`: short-name index first, then FQN. The stored-row and MetadataService steps before it are keyed by the requested name. So for a non-legacy object the by-name read serves the same item the list held under that name, and the verdict is unchanged; for a legacy `ns__short` object addressed by its short name, the gate now judges that object's `enable`, where the list keyed by declared name found nothing and passed the op through to an engine that resolves the alias. The data door has judged that alias since #27897. An ambiguous short name resolves the same way on both doors (first match, warned). No object that passed legitimately is newly refused: an exposed object passes under either name (pinned, two names in one batch), a plain-named restricted object was already refused (pinned). Correct.
4. **The refusal order relative to auth and the credential refusal is unchanged.** The handler's sequence on `main` and on the head is identical outside the gate block: `enforceAuth` → engine presence (501) → schema parse (400) → `atomic` (400) → empty (200) → `enforceBatchSize` → missing-id (400) → the exposure gate → `apiKeyManagementCredentialRefusal` per op (403, after the exposure verdict so an unexposed op keeps its 404/405, before the transaction) → `$ref` resolution inside the transaction. Only the gate block's body moved. Correct.
5. **Fail-open and its log are preserved by the replacement read.** `loadObjectItem` on a thrown by-name read logs the `[REST] api-exposure gate: … failing open` line and answers `undefined`; `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` answers `undefined` silently (the list omitted such an object, so the verdict matches); an absent name answers an empty envelope, so "no object" is silent; a degraded store throws 503 at the protocol and is the logged fail-open. The batch loop treats `undefined` as the old `!obj → continue`. What changes is cardinality: the old code skipped the loop entirely on an empty list (one log per request during an outage); the new code reads each distinct object (one log per distinct object per request). Same verdict, same posture, the dev names it. Accepted; not a defect.
6. **The two #3545 pins still measure a thrown read.** `rest.test.ts`'s `createMockProtocol` has no `getMetaItemForExecution`, so `objectItemReader` takes `getMetaItem`, and the describe-local `setup` defines `getMetaItem` as a read of `getMetaItems` at call time: the mocked rejection of the list reaches the by-name read, the pin asserts `undefined` plus a `warn` containing `api-exposure gate`; the empty-registry pin asserts `undefined` and no `warn`. The assertions are the originals re-pointed, as the claim amendment allowed. Correct.
7. **Dropping the private `loadObjectItems` leaves no caller, static or dynamic.** `git grep` of the whole head tree (including `ui/`, `scripts/`, `dogfood`): the only `loadObjectItems` references are the module-level function in `meta-item-read-gate.ts` (still used by the nav-servability gate and the list fallback) and docblock prose in other packages that names that module function. No string-literal or bracket spelling, no `(rest as any).loadObjectItems` outside the two re-pointed pins, no ADR anchor on the moved text (`rest-server.ts`'s anchor pins `filterAppForUser`, untouched). `BatchRouteHost` is not re-exported from the package entry, so the renamed member is no published type change. Correct.
8. **Public surface.** No route, status, code or body is added or changed; the two refusal envelopes were already published on every `/data/:object` route. The one accept-set change is the narrowing in item 3. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value or type an author can write moves.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/rest` **patch** with a line-initial `**BREAKING**` banner: correct under Post-Task Checklist step 3 (a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition), and the same level the family's merged changeset took. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial exactly once in the PR body and in the changeset body, and match the diff: the arm is a narrowing (an op the door used to write is refused), nothing widens. The ADR-0087 marker is exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate's list holds; its justification is true against the diff (no key added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; no export change; the two refusals are already published). Before / Now / Who sees it / Remedy are each true against the code: the remedy correctly says the short name now answers as the full name does, and names lifting the `enable` restriction as the fix. Title carries `!`. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is present with its `git grep` evidence. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on `2019e190`, read at 2026-10-30T05:29Z:** 47 runs; 33 success (among them `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped ·` all four, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`), 13 skipped by the path filter, one shard (`Test Core (4/8)`) still in progress at this read, 0 failed, 0 cancelled. Pending is pending: the seat reads that shard green before any landing act. No governed surface in the file list; `mergeable: true`, state `blocked` (awaiting review and the running shards), base `ed0e71db`.
- **Dev deviations (5), each read against the card thread:** (i) file surface widened before any push, recorded in claim 6514787457's seat amendment, and the diff stays inside that amended list; (ii) the first red run had no metadata store and every gate failed open, the fixture was corrected before the red-first reading, the throwaway debug test never committed, consistent with the head tree (the fixture registers the four `sys_metadata*` objects and says why); (iii) the dev stopped its own build, not another's, as Multi-agent discipline §8 requires; (iv) `origin/main` moved after the branch point, the dev did not merge; the net diff here is read three-dot against the current `origin/main` and GitHub reports `mergeable: true`; (v) no PR assignee, because the harness offered only an MCP write: the PR's assignee mirrors the card's, so the seat sets it through the relay before landing, a seat item, not a code item. `open_questions: []`, none owed.
- **Out-of-scope note from the dev, read:** the fail-open log is now one line per distinct object (① item 5) and the census docblock's sentence was renamed, not re-measured; the renamed sentence still names the method the healthy-control path reaches, which is true on the head. Accepted as notes.
- **Family closure.** PR #27897's records left this door as the last data door with the old read, and the seat's ACCEPT filed #27899 for it. With this diff every door that asks an object's API exposure asks `RestServer#loadObjectItem`: the `/data/:object` routes through `enforceApiAccess`, the per-object bulk routes through the same, the cross-object batch per op. The one non-resolving arm left is `loadObjectItem`'s list fallback for a protocol with no by-name read, which no shipped protocol is.
- **Observation, no carrier, not this PR's debt:** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/meta-overlay-cache.ts` line 7 still describes the hot path as `enforceApiAccess` → `loadObjectItems`, stale since the by-name read landed (#24031), outside this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts** — holds against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against. The gate block reads each op's object through the host's `loadObjectItem`, the same member `enforceApiAccess` reads, so the batch judges the object the data door serves for the op's name (`registry.getObject`'s resolution, reached through `readMetaItem` step 3). Dedup is per distinct object for the read and per distinct (object, action) for the verdict, in op order, so cost is bounded by the batch-size cap and the first refusal still answers for the whole batch before the transaction. `undefined` keeps the #3770 pass-through, as before. The `BatchRouteHost` member is typed as the class member, so the host literal and the interface cannot disagree. The credential refusal and `$ref` resolution are untouched and keep their positions. No must-fix.

**packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts** — holds. `loadObjectItem` is the former inline body of `enforceApiAccess`, moved, with `enforceApiAccess` now a caller; the docblock records why the batch door reads through it and what the list lacked. The private list read is gone with its only caller; `metaListSource`'s docblock no longer names the batch route among the list's readers, which is true. The host literal hands the new member and no other. No must-fix.

**packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts** — docblock-only, and the sentence is true on the head: the list is read by the nav-servability gate and by the by-name read's fallback; every data door's exposure gate reads by name. No must-fix.

**packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts** — the two re-pointed pins still measure a thrown read and a silent empty registry on the replacement member (① item 6). No must-fix.

**packages/rest/src/objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts** — one docblock word; the renamed method is the one the path reaches. No must-fix.

**packages/rest/src/batch-op-exposure-object-read.test.ts** — the pins are the right shape: a real engine, the real protocol, the real routes, the metadata store registered so the gate is live rather than failing open; each refusal asserts status and whole body `toEqual` the data door's or the bulk door's answer for the same name, the transaction spy never called, zero rows counted at the engine; the short-name premise is asserted before it is relied on; controls cover the full name, an exposed object under both names in one batch, and a plain-named restricted object. **Should-fix (test-side, not blocking):** the suite does not pin the one accept-set answer the replacement read must keep on this door, that an op naming an unregistered object still passes the gate and is answered inside the transaction (the #3770 pass-through). No existing batch test pins it either; the code path is the data door's own, so the risk is low, but the next change to `loadObjectItem`'s absent-name arm would otherwise be caught only on `/data`.

**.changeset/27899-batch-op-exposure-object-read.md** — frontmatter, both declaration lines, one ADR-0087 marker, BREAKING banner, Before / Now / Who sees it / Remedy, each sentence true against the diff; rule-level throughout, no command or fixture reproduced. No must-fix.

No must-fix. The narrowing takes away only an answer that was wrong (a write the data door would have refused under the same name), and makes the spec's own refusal (ADR-0049 `enable.apiEnabled` / `apiMethods`) real on the last data door that read differently.

## 维护者速读

- 为什么改：这是 #27728 / #27729 那一族里最后一个和 `/data` 回答不一致的数据入口（#27899）。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`），只影响用短名访问的旧式 `ns__short` 对象；暴露的对象不论全名短名照常通过，拒绝顺序不变。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`batch-routes.ts` 的逐条暴露检查，以及 `rest-server.ts` 里两道检查共用的私有读取方法。

- 需要你做的：无（非受管；契约复审 PASS 6515741450；席位按本任落地授权落地）。

席位意见：ACCEPT。

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `2019e190f5c40af31fbabccf6fb2d5a3fa612e28`

- **Shape:** every `/batch` op kind reads its object through the private read `enforceApiAccess` now also calls (`RestServer#loadObjectItem`, `registry.getObject` with the legacy short-name resolution) and refuses through the unchanged `apiAccessDenialFromEnable(…, 'bulk', { bulkChild })`, so status, code and envelope equal the `/data` door's; the refusal order (auth → parse → size → missing id → exposure → per-op credential refusal → transaction) is unchanged; fail-open with a log on a thrown read is kept (one log per distinct object per request); the private list read `loadObjectItems` is dropped with no remaining caller. Changeset `@objectstack/rest` patch with a BREAKING note and ADR-0087 disposition, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `check-governed-merges --pr 27963`: NOT governed, 324 changed lines.
- **Premise measured:** red first on base 5 failed / 4 passed, after 9/9; ablation turns the same 5 red, restored to HEAD's blob; `@objectstack/rest` 351 files / 6775 tests; dogfood battery green (dev report 6515574134 on #27899). Rule-level only on public surfaces.
- **Gate check-runs on the head:** 48 runs, 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure/pending; `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Contract review:** PASS, record 6515741450 on this head, no must-fix. Its one should-fix (a pin that an op naming an unregistered object still passes the gate and is answered inside the transaction) is not on this head; the dev wrote it and parked it unpushed for a later card.
